summary: CLI review completed for species-parser retirement and Azure Trusted Signing wiring. Retired identifiers are absent after refreshing the ignored build output; the live species bridge, all five overlay/tooling commands, controller parse, PowerShell parse, six requested .NET verifiers, workflow YAML structure/permissions/order, package Trusted Signing route, and six-secret runbook checks passed. The new workflow has two release-blocking GitHub Actions defects: direct secret use in step if conditions and step-level signing variables that shadow the prepared GITHUB_ENV values.

critical.endpoint: .github/workflows/release-package.yml — Log in to Azure / Prepare Azure Trusted Signing client
critical.issue: Both steps use secrets.AZURE_TRUSTED_SIGNING_ACCOUNT directly in if. GitHub's official Actions documentation states secrets cannot be directly referenced in if conditionals; map the secret to a job-level env value and gate on env.AZURE_TRUSTED_SIGNING_ACCOUNT instead.

The package step explicitly sets ISLEY_CODE_SIGN_DLIB and ISLEY_CODE_SIGN_METADATA from repository secrets. Step-level env has higher precedence than values written by the prepare step to GITHUB_ENV, so the generated dlib/metadata paths are replaced (normally with empty values) and Protect-IsleyAuthenticode silently takes the unsigned path.

minor.issue: The runbook says individual developers are eligible without documenting the current geographic availability limitation; Microsoft currently documents individual validation as available only in the USA and Canada. Add an eligibility/region caveat to prevent a provisioning dead end.

action_items: Map AZURE_TRUSTED_SIGNING_ACCOUNT into jobs.package.env and change both signing-step gates to if: ${{ env.AZURE_TRUSTED_SIGNING_ACCOUNT != '' }}.
Remove the package step's ISLEY_CODE_SIGN_DLIB and ISLEY_CODE_SIGN_METADATA overrides, or restructure fallback handling so values exported by Prepare Azure Trusted Signing client are not shadowed.
Re-run the regression pytest and all overlay checks after fixing the workflow; specifically require both currently failing workflow tests to pass.
Add the current individual identity-validation geography limitation to the provisioning runbook.
critical_code_review_comments: The workflow looks structurally correct under a generic YAML parser but is not semantically valid GitHub Actions because secrets are forbidden directly in if; CI workflow review needs an Actions-aware validation step.
Writing values to GITHUB_ENV is ineffective when a later step redeclares the same names in step env. This causes a dangerous silent unsigned-release fallback rather than a signing failure.
Pin Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client to a reviewed version instead of installing an unconstrained latest package in the release job for reproducibility and release-chain safety.

success_rate.backend: 80% (8/10 focused pytest checks; all five overlay tools and all six requested .NET verifiers passed)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Desktop CLI-only repo; do not start services/browser. The ignored BurntHud/bin copy initially contained the retired parser chain, but dotnet build refreshed Map/isley-map-controller.js before ending with the known benign Linux MSB3030 missing Isley.VoiceServer.exe artifact; source and current ignored output are now clean. Focused pytest has exactly two failures, both in release-package.yml. Actual Azure signing remains intentionally untested due to missing Azure credentials.
rca_of_the_issue: Workflow RCA: GitHub Actions forbids direct secrets references in if conditionals (official guidance: https://docs.github.com/actions/security-guides/using-secrets-in-github-actions). Independently, GitHub env precedence makes step-level env more specific than inherited job/GITHUB_ENV state; Package Windows archives redeclares both generated path variables, replacing the values exported on lines 72-73. As a result the OIDC steps are invalidly gated and, once that is corrected, the signing inputs would still be empty and packaging would silently skip Authenticode signing. Reproduction: run pytest /app/tests/test_release_signing_and_species_retirement.py; test_signing_gate_uses_supported_env_context and test_prepared_signing_paths_are_not_shadowed_on_package_step fail deterministically.
